newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 4.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Friday.
- Irish interest rates may fall before the end of 1996 as overseas money is being pumped into Dublin financial markets in anticipation of Ireland's entry into EMU.
- Irish police seized files from a solicitor in Dublin whose client is a main suspect in the murder of crime journalist Veronica Guerin.
- Irish health insurer VHI is expected to appoint an interim chief executive on Friday until a permanent candidate is found.
- Irish monetary statistics released on Thursday showed that consumer borrowing continues to rise and economists say that the Irish central bank has lost the power to do anything about it.

- Insurance services group Norwich Union is still accepting customers for life and pensions policies who will qualify for free shares in the planned two billion pounds sterling flotation, even though the deadline expired on October 2.
- Three-quarters of Irish voters believe Ireland should join EMU in 1999, an Irish Times/MRBI poll showed on Friday.

- An English rugby player who collapsed after scoring a try in a friendly match in County Galway, later died in hospital from a combination of alcohol, the drug ecstasy and physical exertion, an inquest was told.
- Stale-owned Irish credit institution ICC is to cut its workforce by 10 percent in a voluntary redendancy plan.
- There are fresh hopes of a natural gas find off the coast of County Mayo after exploration company Enterprise Oil discovered traces of gas in well tests.
- Lending by banks in the Irish financial services centre will soon exceed the Irish domestic banking sector total, the Customs House Docks Development said on Thursday.
- Ireland's largest mortgage lender Irish Permanent cut its five-year fixed-rate mortgage by half a percent to 7.25 percent on Thursday.
